newsitem.title: USA: CBOT traders see no corn deliveries on September.
newsitem.headline: CBOT traders see no corn deliveries on September.

text.p: CBOT traders including cash-connected firms expect no corn to be posted Friday, first notice day for delivery on the September contract.
"No corn deliveries, the basis is strong and there really are no deliverable supplies," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.
Haugens and others acknowledged the U.S. Midwest corn basis market recently fell hard as early harvested corn from the South moved to select processors in the Midwest.
But the basis market remains strong relative to the CBOT September contract price which will discourage deliveries.
"The basis has come down dramatically but it's still high relative to the board," a cash-connected trader said.

Also as of late Tuesday, there were only 20,000 bushels of corn in Chicago registered for possible delivery and none in Toledo or St Louis, according to the CBOT. Traders said the tight supply alone will prevent much corn from entering the delivery cycle.
Soybean deliveries also are expected to be light, from zero to 200,000 bushels, they said.
"No corn and insignificant beans, maybe nothing to 200,000 bushels," the cash trader said.
As of late Tuesday there were 170,000 bushels of soybeans registered in Chicago for potential delivery and 5,000 in Toledo.
Traders said the tight supply of soybeans plus a cash basis market that remains firm relative to the September futures contract price will keep soybeans out of the delivery market.
Also, no soymeal was expected to surface in the delivery market with soyoil deliveries estimated at from 1,000 to 2,000 lots.
As of late Tuesday, 2,257 lots of soyoil were registered and 398 lots of soymeal.
"No corn, meal or beans with wheat at three to five million (bushels) or more," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds, projecting deliveries.
Traders said wheat deliveries could be heavy on the increased supply of wheat in Toledo and on a slowdown in export demand for U.S. wheat.
As of late Tuesday, wheat registered in Toledo for possible delivery totaled 1,989,776 bushels and 61,609 bushels were registered in Chicago.
Oat deliveries on the September were estimated at one to two mln bushels. There were 1,470,000 bushels of oats registered in Minneapolis as of late Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
